acceptance: Re-run the original reproduction (a delegated task making a relative-path edit of a tracked file in the primary clone while a worktree is active) in omp and in Claude Code with the PR #4143 hook in place, and record the result here. If both refuse, the remaining scope is only agents or tools that bypass the hook (see codex-apply-patch-skips-pretooluse-hook-20261117).

Decision gate: the owner picks the mechanism for the remaining scope from a written comparison of the options (read-only tracked files, a path-refusing hook, a check around each delegated task), recorded here before implementation.
Pass rubric for the reproduction: the write is refused before it lands, or reported in the same tool result with the path named, and afterwards git -C <primary clone> status --short is empty.
The chosen mechanism is documented in docs/agent/primary-clone-guard.md, including why the alternatives were not chosen.
Guardrails: no change blocks the owner's own edits in the primary clone; BENCHBOX_ALLOW_MAIN_CLONE_WRITE=1 still bypasses for emergency writes; nothing relies on the agent remembering an instruction.
context: 2026-11-17: related coverage since this item was filed: PR #4143 added the pre-tool write guard hook (enforced in omp and Claude Code, not called by Codex for apply_patch: codex-apply-patch-skips-pretooluse-hook-20261117), and PR #4265 (04929364fb) made make agent-write-preflight also report new untracked, non-ignored files in the primary clone. A subagent whose file tool bypasses the hook is still caught only after the fact.
description:
Defect in the safety net. On 2026-11-12 a subagent working in its own worktree edited `tests/unit/scripts/explorer_pipeline/test_duckdb_builder.py` in the primary clone, because its file tool resolved a relative path against the session directory. `docs/agent/primary-clone-guard.md` describes this hazard, and `scripts/check_primary_clone_clean.sh report` only reports. The edit was found by chance through `git status` before a batch step that refuses a dirty primary clone; the same change was also missing from the agent's worktree, so its tests had been passing without it.

Expected: an agent write to a tracked path in the primary clone is refused or surfaced at the time of the write, not at a later unrelated gate. Options to evaluate: make the primary clone's tracked files read-only for agent sessions, a file-tool hook that refuses relative or primary-clone paths when a worktree is active, or a cheap check at the start and end of every delegated task.

Guardrails: must not block the owner's own edits or the documented `BENCHBOX_ALLOW_MAIN_CLONE_WRITE=1` emergency path. Must not rely on the agent remembering an instruction; the instruction was given and still failed.
